items.name: Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew (Emerald Buddha)
items.nameThai: พระบรมมหาราชวัง และวัดพระแก้ว
items.description: The old royal palace and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha share one walled compound by the river: gold spires, painted galleries and throne halls. It is the busiest sight in Bangkok, so come when it opens. Wat Pho is next door and Wat Arun is a short ferry ride away.
items.openText: Daily 8:30-15:30 for entry (ticket sales end at 15:30); the grounds close at 16:30. It can close at short notice for royal ceremonies.
items.feeText: 500 THB for foreigners. The ticket includes Wat Phra Kaew and the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles. Buy at the gate or online on the official site.
items.bestTime: 8:30, at opening, before the tour groups and the midday heat.
items.gettingThere: Chao Phraya Express Boat to Tha Chang pier (N9), then 5-10 minutes on foot. Or MRT Sanam Chai, then 10-15 minutes on foot past Wat Pho.
tips: Strict dress code: no sleeveless, see-through or crop tops, no shorts or mini skirts, no ripped, tight or cycling trousers. Wear long trousers or a long skirt and a T-shirt with sleeves.
The palace is open every day. If someone outside says it is closed today and offers a cheap tuk-tuk tour, walk on: it is the gem-shop scam.
Drones are not allowed.

The royal cremation of Queen Mother Sirikit is at Sanam Luang, next to the palace, on 15-19 Dec 2026. In 2017 the royal crematorium was opened to the public after the King's cremation. If that happens again, expect queues and closed roads around Sanam Luang in early January 2027. Check the official site the day before.
Do the Grand Palace first, then Wat Pho, then take the ferry to Wat Arun for the late light.

items.name: Wat Pho (Reclining Buddha)
items.nameThai: วัดพระเชตุพนวิมลมังคลาราม (วัดโพธิ์)
items.description: The temple next to the Grand Palace, home of the huge gold Reclining Buddha and a well-known Thai massage school. It is calmer than the palace and stays open into the evening.
items.openText: Daily 8:00-19:30 (Google Maps; the temple's own site gives 08:30-19:30).
items.feeText: 300 THB for foreigners. Thai massage at the temple school costs extra: recent guides give about 340 THB for 30 minutes and about 520 THB for 1 hour; check the price board.
items.bestTime: After 16:00, when the tour groups leave; you can stay until 19:30.
items.gettingThere: Chao Phraya boat to Tha Tien pier (N8), about 300 m away. MRT Sanam Chai is about 350 m away. From the Grand Palace walk about 10 minutes south.
tips: Cover your shoulders; women should not wear shorts above the knee (temple rule).
Massage is walk-in and the pavilions get busy in the afternoon.
The ferry to Wat Arun leaves from Tha Tien pier, a few minutes' walk away.

items.name: Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn)
items.nameThai: วัดอรุณราชวราราม
items.description: The riverside temple across from Wat Pho, with a tall central prang covered in pieces of Chinese porcelain. You can climb part of the steep steps for a view over the river to the Grand Palace. At sunset it is the classic view from the opposite bank.
items.openText: Daily 8:00-18:00; last entry about 17:30. The prang closes to climbers a little earlier.
items.feeText: 200 THB, cash only at the gate; there is no official online ticket. The cross-river ferry costs a few baht. Sarong rental about 20 THB plus a 100 THB deposit.
items.bestTime: 8:00-9:00, or 15:30-17:30 for the light. Then watch the sunset (about 18:05-18:15 in January) from the Tha Tien side.
items.gettingThere: Cross-river ferry from Tha Tien pier next to Wat Pho, about 3 minutes, roughly 5:00-19:00. From BTS Saphan Taksin take the express boat upriver to Tha Tien first.
tips: Shoulders and knees must be covered; the rule is enforced more strictly than at Wat Pho.
Bring small notes: the ticket booth and the ferry often cannot change 1,000 THB notes.
Do not climb the prang in flip-flops; the steps are steep and slippery after rain.
Riverside cafes on the Tha Tien side have upper terraces facing the temple for sunset.

items.name: Golden Mount (Wat Saket)
items.nameThai: ภูเขาทอง วัดสระเกศ
items.description: A gold chedi on top of an artificial hill in the old town, reached by 344 steps on a gentle slope with places to rest. The top terrace has a 360-degree view over old Bangkok. It is quieter than the big three temples and best near sunset.
items.openText: Daily about 7:30-19:00 (Google Maps says from 7:00).
items.feeText: 100 THB.
items.bestTime: 16:30 to sunset (about 18:05-18:15 in January).
items.gettingThere: Grab or taxi, or the Khlong Saen Saep canal boat to Phan Fa Lilat pier, a short walk away. Thipsamai pad thai is about 200 m away and Khao San Road about 1.2 km.
tips: Cover shoulders, belly and knees; men should not wear tank tops.
Wear shoes you can climb stairs in.
Good plan: Golden Mount at sunset, then dinner at Thipsamai.

items.name: Yaowarat (Chinatown) night food
items.nameThai: ถนนเยาวราช
items.description: Chinatown's main road turns into a long open-air food street every evening. Eat peppery rolled-noodle soup (guay jub), grilled seafood, noodles and desserts at stalls and old shophouses, several of them in the Michelin Guide at normal prices. Go hungry and share dishes as a group.
items.openText: Stalls run from about 17:00-18:00 to midnight. Many stalls take Monday off.
items.feeText: Free to walk. A bowl of guay jub costs about 60-100 THB; seafood restaurants cost more. Bring cash.
items.bestTime: 19:00-22:00, Tuesday to Sunday.
items.gettingThere: MRT Wat Mangkon, about 250 m from the corner of Yaowarat Road and Soi Texas (Phadung Dao Road).
tips: Nai Ek Roll Noodles (Yaowarat Soi 9): guay jub with crispy pork, open about 7:30-00:30 daily.
Guay Jub Ouan Pochana (408 Yaowarat Rd): very peppery guay jub, 10:30-24:00, closed Monday.
T&K Seafood and Lek Seafood face each other at the Soi Texas corner, from 16:00 to about midnight and 2:00.
Bar Temp., a vinyl house and techno bar, is about 500 m away (Wednesday to Sunday).
Keep phones and wallets in front pockets in the crowd.

items.name: Talat Noi (old riverside quarter)
items.nameThai: ตลาดน้อย
items.description: A small riverside quarter next to Chinatown: narrow lanes, old Chinese houses, mechanic workshops, street art and cafes by the water. Look for the So Heng Tai mansion, the Holy Rosary Church (built 1891-1897) and the Chow Sue Kong shrine (about 1804). It fits well before an evening in Yaowarat.
items.openText: Streets always open. The Talat Noi Museum is free and closed on Monday.
items.feeText: Free to walk around.
items.bestTime: 15:30-18:30, then sunset by the river and dinner in Yaowarat.
items.gettingThere: About 10 minutes on foot from MRT Hua Lamphong, or 10-15 minutes from MRT Wat Mangkon.
tips: Hong Sieng Kong cafe has a shaded river terrace and live music in the evening.
Clutch, a vinyl bar with big JBL speakers in The Warehouse on Charoen Krung, opens 18:00-2:00 (closed Monday); cover up to about 300 THB.
People live and work here: keep the lanes clear and ask before photographing people.

items.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market (JJ)
items.nameThai: ตลาดนัดจตุจักร
items.description: A huge weekend market with more than 15,000 stalls in 27 sections: clothes, vintage, art, homeware, plants and street food. On Saturday and Sunday everything is open; on other days only small parts are. It gets very hot and crowded after midday.
items.openText: Whole market Sat-Sun 9:00-18:00. Friday 18:00-24:00 wholesale only. Wednesday and Thursday 7:00-18:00 plant section only.
items.feeText: Free entry. Bring cash and small notes.
items.bestTime: Saturday or Sunday 9:00-11:00.
items.gettingThere: MRT Kamphaeng Phet (about 350 m) or MRT Chatuchak Park (about 2 minutes to Entrance 2); BTS Mo Chit is next to Chatuchak Park.
tips: On weekdays it is not worth the trip: go to Jodd Fairs in the evening instead.
Cool down in the air-conditioned MIXT Chatuchak and JJ Mall next door (about 10:00-20:00 daily).
Agree a meeting point and a time before the group splits up.

items.name: Jodd Fairs Ratchada (night market)
items.nameThai: จ๊อดแฟร์ รัชดา
items.description: Bangkok's busiest night market for eating, with about 800 stalls, mostly food, plus bars and live music. Try leng saap, a big pile of spicy pork spine in sour broth, and grilled seafood. The old Rama 9 and DanNeramit sites have closed; this is the only Jodd Fairs now.
items.feeText: Free entry. Leng saap from 180 THB (medium, enough for two). Dinner for two about 600-1,200 THB with drinks. Most stalls take cash or Thai QR only.
items.bestTime: 17:30-19:00 for free tables and short queues; on Friday and Saturday after 20:00 it is packed.
items.gettingThere: MRT Thailand Cultural Centre exit 4, about 3 minutes on foot, next to Big C Place Ratchada. The MRT stops around midnight, so take Grab back if you stay late.
tips: Some map apps still show the closed Rama 9 site. Go to Ratchadaphisek Road, next to Big C.
Order leng saap one size smaller than you think.
The RCA clubs are about 2 km away.

items.name: Sky Bar at lebua (State Tower)
items.description: The open-air bar on the 64th floor of State Tower, with a glowing round bar above the river view. It became famous from The Hangover Part II. Drinks cost about 1,300-1,500 THB before tax, so go once for the sunset view, then drink elsewhere.
items.openText: Daily 17:00-00:30; last drink order 00:15.
items.feeText: No entry fee, but each person must buy at least one drink. Cocktails 1,300-1,500 THB, mocktails 900 THB, wine from 980 THB a glass, plus 10% service and 7% VAT (drink list, Oct 2026).
items.bestTime: Arrive 17:15-17:45 for the sunset (about 18:05-18:15 in January).
items.gettingThere: About 400 m (5-6 minutes) on foot from BTS Saphan Taksin and Sathorn pier.
tips: Smart casual: no sleeveless shirts for men, no sportswear, flip-flops or swimwear. No large bags; there is no storage.
Walk-in only, no reservations. Photos are allowed, video is not.
Cheaper rooftops: Octave at Thong Lo (cocktails about 525-555 THB) or Bar.Yard at the Kimpton Maa-Lai, BK Magazine's best rooftop bar for 2026.

items.name: Octave Rooftop Bar (Thong Lo)
items.description: A rooftop bar on floors 45 to 49 of the Bangkok Marriott Sukhumvit, with an open 360-degree deck on top. Drinks cost less than half of Sky Bar's, it stays open to 2:00 and it is next to the Thonglor bars. DJs play house from about 21:00.
items.feeText: No entry fee; at least one drink each. Cocktails about 525-555 THB, local beer 290-320 THB, plus 10% service and 7% VAT. Happy hour 17:00-19:00 with 50% off selected drinks (July 2026).
items.bestTime: 17:00-17:30 to get a sunset seat on the 49th floor.
items.gettingThere: BTS Thong Lo, about 250 m (3-4 minutes) on foot. The hotel is at Sukhumvit Soi 57.
tips: Floors 48 and 49 are for guests aged 20 and over; bring ID.
Smart casual: no sportswear, flip-flops or sleeveless tops for men.

items.name: Mahanakhon SkyWalk (glass floor, 78th floor)
items.nameThai: มหานคร สกายวอล์ค
items.description: Thailand's highest observation deck, 314 m up on the King Power Mahanakhon tower in Silom. A fast lift goes to an indoor deck on the 74th floor; above it the open roof on the 78th floor has a glass floor 310 m above the street. Go before sunset and stay for the city lights.
items.openText: Daily 10:00-24:00; last entry 23:00.
items.feeText: Adults 1,000 THB from 10:00 to 15:30 and 1,200 THB from 15:30 to 19:00 on the official site; the later evening price is not listed. Resellers such as Klook sell tickets from about US$30.
items.bestTime: Arrive about 17:00 for the sunset (about 18:05-18:15 in January) and the night view.
items.gettingThere: BTS Chong Nonsi, exit 3.
tips: The 78th-floor rooftop has a bar if you want a drink with the view.
Elsewhere (after-hours bar) is about 150 m from BTS Chong Nonsi, and the Decho Road clubs are about 10 minutes on foot.

items.name: Thonglor and Ekkamai (bars and small clubs)
items.nameThai: ทองหล่อ / เอกมัย
items.description: Two parallel side streets off Sukhumvit, Thonglor (Soi 55) and Ekkamai (Soi 63), with many cocktail bars, rooftops, restaurants and mid-size clubs. The crowds dress up. Thonglor is not a 4am zone, so most places close at 2:00.
items.openText: Bars from about 17:00-18:00; clubs from about 21:00 or 23:00 to 2:00.
items.feeText: Club covers about 600-1,200 THB.
items.bestTime: Thursday to Saturday; clubs fill after 23:00.
items.gettingThere: BTS Thong Lo or BTS Ekkamai. Thonglor is about 2.5 km long, so use Grab or a motorbike taxi to move up and down it.
tips: 12 x 12 (Ekkamai) is a community-run room of about 50 people for house, techno, disco and jazz, open since 2014 (Tue-Sat 18:00-2:00).
MUIN, on the 5th floor of Donki Mall Thonglor, is a big Korean-style club with separate EDM, hip-hop and house-techno rooms (Wed-Sun from 21:00).
Loopliner (Aug 2026) reports a new hard-techno room, Berlin BKK, in the same mall. It is not on Google Maps yet, so check its Instagram first.
Good order: Octave rooftop at sunset, beef soup at Wattana Panich before 19:00, then bars and clubs.
Dress: collared shirt and real shoes, no flip-flops.
Older guides list Beam and De Commune here; both have closed.

items.name: Sukhumvit Soi 11 and Asok (big clubs)
items.nameThai: ซอยสุขุมวิท 11 / อโศก
items.description: The street with the most clubs in the city, a short walk from BTS Nana, and the easiest first night out: tourists, expats and locals, hip-hop and EDM, covers that usually include a drink. Apt 101 on Sukhumvit Road near Asok won BK Magazine's best nightclub award for 2026. It is fun but not underground.
items.openText: Clubs open about 22:00 and close at 3:00-4:00 (Levels to 3:00, Sugar Club to 4:00 on Google Maps). Apt 101: Tue-Sun 20:00-2:00.
items.feeText: Covers about 300-600 THB, usually with one drink; weeknights are often free.
items.bestTime: Friday or Saturday after 23:00.
items.gettingThere: BTS Nana, about 400 m. Apt 101 is about 200 m from BTS Asok.
tips: Levels (6th floor of the Aloft hotel): a big club with three areas.
Sugar Club: hip-hop every night since 2014; the crowd dresses up.
Apt 101 (3rd floor, 233 Sukhumvit Rd): a 1970s-penthouse-style club with cocktails and disco and house nights.

Insanity on Soi 11 has closed, though some guides still list it.
For underground techno go to Decho Road (Mustache, Subwerk) instead.

items.name: RCA (Royal City Avenue): superclubs and VOID
items.nameThai: อาร์ซีเอ (รอยัลซิตี้อเวนิว)
items.description: A short avenue of very large clubs east of the centre, such as Onyx and Route 66, with festival-size sound and lasers. VOID, next to it, plays techno, progressive house and big-room and entered DJ Mag's Top 100 Clubs at number 67 in 2026. RCA is one of the zones where licensed clubs may stay open to 4:00.
items.openText: Clubs nightly from about 21:00-22:00 to 4:00 (Route 66 and Onyx to 4:00, VOID to 3:45 on Google Maps). INAKOMA: Fridays 22:00-4:00.
items.feeText: Entry depends on the night and the DJ. INAKOMA hard-techno Fridays cost about 300-400 THB with free beer from 22:00 to 24:00.
items.bestTime: Friday or Saturday after midnight.
items.gettingThere: Grab or taxi is easiest. MRT Phra Ram 9 is about 1.2 km away (15 minutes on foot).
tips: Bring your original passport, not a copy: door staff check ID closely.

Route 66 has several rooms: hip-hop, EDM and house, and live bands.
Jodd Fairs night market is about 2 km away for dinner first.

items.name: Ari (cafes, food and small bars)
items.nameThai: อารีย์
items.description: A leafy, relaxed neighbourhood north of the centre, popular with young Thais for coffee, brunch and Thai food, with a handful of small bars at night. There are no big clubs. Come for a slow afternoon, an early dinner or live music.
items.openText: Cafes from the morning; bars in the evening.
items.feeText: Free to walk around.
items.bestTime: Late afternoon into the evening; weekend brunch.
items.gettingThere: BTS Ari, exit 3 for Soi Ari, where most cafes are.
tips: Bar Luk Krung: live bands playing classic Thai songs, with cocktails made from local flavours.

items.name: Khao San Road (backpacker street)
items.nameThai: ถนนข้าวสาร
items.description: The famous backpacker street in the old town: open-air bars, buckets of cocktails, dancing on tables, street food and loud music. Fun to see for one night, and close to the Grand Palace and the Rajadamnern stadium. The music is mostly commercial, not underground.
items.openText: Busy every night. Khao San is not a 4am zone, so most bars close around 2:00; a few licensed clubs, such as The Club, list later hours.
items.feeText: Free to walk.
items.gettingThere: No BTS or MRT nearby. Chao Phraya boat to Phra Arthit pier (about 600 m), or Grab. Rajadamnern Stadium is about 1.3 km away and Thipsamai about 1 km.
tips: Police raided an unlicensed club on Khao San (OK Bar) on 10 Oct 2026 and tested the guests: 31 of 102 were positive for drugs. Do not take anything.
The Club Khaosan, number 71 in DJ Mag's Top 100 Clubs 2026, opens nightly from about 21:00.
Check drink prices before you order.

items.name: Mustache Bangkok (house and techno club)
items.description: A finalist for best nightclub in BK Magazine's 2026 awards, which call it the place for proper ravers and techno heads. A 700-capacity room on Decho Road in Silom with a VOID sound system and regular international DJs. The music is melodic techno, house and tech house; the team dropped hard techno in 2025.
items.openText: Friday and Saturday only: doors 22:00, close 3:30.
items.feeText: Usually presale 350 THB, door 500 THB, both with one drink before midnight. Special nights 500-1,700 THB.
items.bestTime: Arrive by 23:30 so the free drink counts; the floor is fullest after 1:00.
items.gettingThere: Decho Road, just off Surawong Road: about 600 m (8-10 minutes) on foot from BTS Chong Nonsi or 800 m from MRT Sam Yan.
tips: 20+ with real ID (passport). No swim shorts, singlets or flip-flops.
Subwerk (hard techno) is in the same spot on Decho Road, and Elsewhere for after-hours is about 650 m away.
The calendar changes fast and some nights move to other venues (in Sept 2026 two nights were at ABUN dance on Sukhumvit Soi 11). Check the website the week you go.

items.name: Subwerk (hard techno and psytrance)
items.description: A 350-capacity club on Decho Road run by Rave Times, the city's biggest techno community. It plays hard techno at 150-160 BPM and psytrance with weekly international guests, and has no tables and no dress code. It calls itself Bangkok's hardest underground club.
items.openText: Friday and Saturday 22:00-3:00.
items.feeText: Early bird 330 THB, presale 400 THB, door 500 THB; no drink included (Oct 2026).
items.bestTime: After midnight.
items.gettingThere: Same spot on Decho Road as Mustache: about 600 m (8-10 minutes) on foot from BTS Chong Nonsi.
tips: 20+, ID or passport checked at the door.
The club asks guests not to smoke weed in front of the club; cannabis flower is a controlled drug in Thailand now.
Mustache and Subwerk sometimes sell one ticket for both clubs.
Rave Times also runs a monthly techno pool party at Centara Grand at CentralWorld (next on Sat 21 Nov 2026); check for a January date.

items.description: A small after-hours bar on the 9th floor of Trinity Complex in Silom, with a strong sound system and cocktails. items.feeText: Cover depends on the night; check the RA listing.
items.gettingThere: Trinity Complex, Soi Naradhiwas 3 in Silom: about 150 m from BTS Chong Nonsi and about 650 m from Decho Road.
tips: It is a small room (about 60-100 people), so a group of eight should arrive together.

items.name: Rajadamnern Stadium (Muay Thai every night)
items.nameThai: เวทีมวยราชดำเนิน
items.description: The stadium that calls itself the world's first Muay Thai stadium, on Ratchadamnoen Nok Road in the old town, with fights every night. Saturday is RWS (Rajadamnern World Series), the biggest show: three-round bouts, a five-round main event and free-flowing beer. Other nights have traditional cards.
items.openText: Fights every night. Mon, Tue and Fri: Rajadamnern Knockout; Wed: New Power; Thu: Petchyindee; Sun: Kiatpetch (doors 17:00-18:00). Sat: RWS, doors 18:00.

items.bestTime: Saturday RWS for the full show; arrive by 19:00.
items.gettingThere: 8 Ratchadamnoen Nok Road: about 1.3 km (15-20 minutes) on foot from Khao San Road, or Grab.
tips: Book RWS ahead on the official site; Saturdays sell out.

items.description: The 9,500-seat national Muay Thai stadium, now on Ram Intra Road in the north of the city. Every Friday ONE Championship runs ONE Friday Fights, about 14 bouts of Muay Thai, kickboxing and MMA, streamed live. Saturdays have the Lumpinee Stadium Championship.

items.description: A pad thai shop in the old town that reviews often call the original, with queues every evening. The signature is pad thai wrapped in a thin egg, cooked over high heat at the front, with fresh orange juice. Jay Fai, the street cook with a Michelin star, is a few doors away.

items.name: Ayutthaya day trip (old capital ruins)
items.nameThai: พระนครศรีอยุธยา
items.description: The ruins of the old capital, listed by UNESCO as the Historic City of Ayutthaya, about 75 minutes north of Bangkok by train. Brick prangs and old temples fill the island, including Wat Mahathat with its Buddha head in tree roots and Wat Chaiwatthanaram on the far bank. Rent bikes or a tuk-tuk to get around.
items.openText: Temples daily about 8:00-18:00; Wat Mahathat to 18:30.
items.feeText: 80 THB per major temple, or 300 THB for a 7-temple pass. Train about 20-50 THB each way; Grab about 900 THB per car each way.
items.bestTime: Leave Bangkok 7:00-9:00; the ruins are very hot from 11:00 to 15:00.
items.gettingThere: From Krung Thep Aphiwat (Bang Sue): Bangkok Connex train, 75 minutes, at 09:05 and 18:15 daily and 05:15 on weekdays (50 THB launch fare until 31 Oct 2026, so it may change); or one of about 16 long-distance trains, 50-80 minutes, about 20 THB in third class. Slow trains from Hua Lamphong take 1.5-2 hours. Vans from Mo Chit 2: 150-220 THB. Grab about 900 THB per car.
tips: From Ayutthaya station take the 10 THB ferry to the island and rent bikes there (60-100 THB a day); the last boat is around 17:30.
Ride Wat Mahathat, Wat Ratchaburana and Wat Phra Si Sanphet in the middle, then Wat Chaiwatthanaram after lunch.
Back to Bangkok: Bangkok Connex at 14:40 or 19:45, or the 16:48 day train.
Temple dress rules apply: cover shoulders and knees.

items.name: Damnoen Saduak floating market and Maeklong railway market
items.nameThai: ตลาดน้ำดำเนินสะดวก และตลาดร่มหุบแม่กลอง
items.description: Two classic morning sights about 1.5-2 hours south-west of Bangkok. At Damnoen Saduak, vendors sell food from boats on narrow canals; it is popular with tour groups, so go early. At Maeklong, stalls sit on the railway line and pull back their awnings minutes before the train passes.
items.openText: Damnoen Saduak: mornings, about 7:00-13:00. Maeklong trains arrive at 08:30, 11:10, 14:30 and 17:40 and leave at 06:20, 09:00, 11:30 and 15:30.
items.feeText: No entry fee. Boats at Damnoen Saduak are priced per boat: a rowing boat about 300-400 THB, a longtail about 600 THB for about an hour at Yuwanda Pier. Shared tours from Bangkok start at about US$18 per person.
items.bestTime: Leave Bangkok by 6:30-7:00: Damnoen Saduak by 8:00-9:00, then Maeklong for the 11:10 train (or Maeklong first for the 08:30 train).
items.gettingThere: Easiest with a tour, or a private van with driver for the group. Public transport: buses from Bangkok's Southern Bus Terminal to Damnoen Saduak; Maeklong by train needs two trains and a ferry via Maha Chai. The two markets are about 13 km apart in a straight line.
tips: Before you pay for a boat, agree whether the price is per boat or per person, the route and the time.
Touts at the bus drop-off may say a boat tour is the only way to see the market; you can walk past them.
At Maeklong stand clear of the rails and follow the stall-holders.
Bring cash in small notes.

items.name: Bang Krachao (cycling the green lung)
items.nameThai: บางกะเจ้า
items.description: Bangkok's 'green lung': a loop of the Chao Phraya River with parks and quiet lanes, a short boat ride from Khlong Toei. Rent bikes at the landing and ride to Sri Nakhon Khuean Khan Park. A slow, green half-day that feels far from the city.
items.openText: Ferry daily 6:00-20:00; park 5:00-19:00; bike shops about 8:00-18:00. Bang Nam Phueng floating market: Saturday and Sunday 7:30-16:00.
items.feeText: Ferry 10-20 THB each way; bikes 30-80 THB a day; the park is free.

items.gettingThere: MRT Khlong Toei, then a short Grab (or a 30-minute walk) to Wat Khlong Toei Nok pier. Cross by boat; bikes are at the landing.
tips: Keep your return ferry ticket.
Pay the posted fare: 20 THB on the big boat or 10 THB on the small one each way.
Bring water and sunscreen.

essentials.title: Getting to Bangkok from Phuket
essentials.text: Fly. The flight takes 1 h 20 min to 1 h 45 min, with about 50-60 nonstop flights a day from about 06:30 to after 23:00. Don Mueang (DMK) has the low-cost airlines Thai AirAsia, Nok Air and Thai Lion Air; Suvarnabhumi (BKK) has THAI, Bangkok Airways, Thai Vietjet and some Thai AirAsia flights. Google Flights on 21 Oct 2026, one way, Fri 15 Jan 2027: Phuket to DMK from 1,608 THB (Thai AirAsia), 1,673 (Nok Air) or 1,995 (Thai Lion Air); Phuket to BKK from 1,694 (Thai Vietjet), 2,411 (Thai AirAsia), 2,530 (Bangkok Airways) or 2,555 (THAI). Back on Sun 17 Jan from 1,502 THB (BKK, Thai Vietjet) or 1,608 THB (DMK). Low-cost fares are before checked bags. If your flight home leaves from BKK, fly into BKK: crossing between the two airports takes 60-90 minutes. Phuket airport is about 50 min by car from Patong, 55-60 min from Kata and 65-75 min from Rawai; add 20-30 min on high-season evenings and arrive 90 min to 2 h before take-off. From Koh Phangan (after 23 Jan): only Bangkok Airways flies Koh Samui to Bangkok, from 5,900 THB on Sat 23 Jan; Surat Thani to DMK starts at 1,500 THB (Thai AirAsia) but needs the boat and a bus first.

essentials.title: From the airport to the city
essentials.text: Suvarnabhumi (BKK): the Airport Rail Link runs 05:30-24:00, every 10-13 minutes, for 15-45 THB; Phaya Thai (for the BTS) is 45 THB and 27 minutes, and Makkasan connects to the MRT. You can tap a contactless bank card at the gates. A taxi to the centre costs about 400-600 THB including the 50 THB airport fee and about 75 THB in tolls, and takes 45 minutes to over an hour; Grab costs about 400-600 THB from Level 1, Gate 4. Don Mueang (DMK): the SRT Red Line from the skywalk on floor 2 costs 33 THB to Krung Thep Aphiwat for the MRT Blue Line (about 05:00-24:00); bus A1 (30 THB) goes to BTS Mo Chit and bus A2 (30 THB) to Victory Monument; a taxi costs about 250-400 THB plus the 50 THB fee and tolls (the Don Mueang Tollway alone is 90 THB). Eight people with bags need two cars or a van.

essentials.title: Getting around Bangkok
essentials.text: BTS Skytrain: buy single tickets or a Rabbit card (100 THB issue fee; bring your passport). Bank cards do not work at BTS gates yet. Fares depend on distance, from 17 THB; trips that run onto the extensions are capped at 65 THB (since 1 Nov 2025). MRT Metro: tap a contactless Visa or Mastercard at the gate (not Apple Pay or Google Pay). Both run about 06:00-24:00, so after clubs use Grab, Bolt or a metered taxi; eight people need two cars. A single 17-45 THB fare for all lines is planned from 1 Jan 2027, but the rules were not final in Oct 2026. River: the Chao Phraya Express Boat (orange flag) costs about 18-19 THB flat; fares changed several times in 2026 with diesel prices, and some daytime runs use other flag colours, so check the flag and its stops at the pier. The blue-flag tourist boat costs 40 THB a ride or 150 THB for a day pass (Jan 2026) and no longer stops at Tha Tien. The cross-river ferry from Tha Tien to Wat Arun costs a few baht. Tuk-tuks: agree the price before you get in.

essentials.title: Where to stay for nightlife
essentials.text: Sukhumvit between Nana/Asok and Thong Lo/Ekkamai is the easiest base: BTS and MRT, the Soi 11 clubs, Thonglor bars and rooftops. The side streets around Nana have a red-light scene. Silom and Sathorn (BTS Sala Daeng or Chong Nonsi, MRT Silom or Sam Yan) are best for the underground clubs: Mustache, Subwerk and Elsewhere are 10-15 minutes on foot, and Sky Bar and the Mahanakhon SkyWalk are close. The Old Town and Khao San are cheap and next to the temples and Rajadamnern, but loud at night and with no train station. The riverside is calm and pretty but has little nightlife. For eight people, book rooms in one hotel or a serviced apartment near a station. Renting a condo apartment for less than 30 days without a hotel licence breaks the Hotel Act and many building rules, and inspections increased in 2025, so choose licensed places.

essentials.title: Club nights: closing times, ID and dress
essentials.text: Closing times in 2026: bars without an entertainment licence close at midnight and licensed clubs at 2:00. Only venues in the Silom, RCA and Ratchadaphisek zones that were licensed before the zone rules may stay open to 4:00; Thonglor closes at 2:00. The old 14:00-17:00 ban on alcohol sales has been lifted. Bring your original passport, not a copy: clubs check ID and the legal drinking age is 20. Covers at the main clubs are about 300-700 THB, often with a drink; presale tickets are cheaper (Mustache 350 instead of 500 THB). Dress: no flip-flops, singlets or swim shorts at Mustache; Thonglor clubs and rooftops want a collared shirt and real shoes; Subwerk has no dress code. BTS and MRT stop around midnight and restart about 06:00, so plan Grab rides home.

essentials.title: Drugs, police raids, cannabis and vapes
essentials.text: Police raid bars and clubs and can order urine tests for every foreign guest. On 5 Jul 2026 more than 100 tourists at two unlicensed bars in Ratchadamri were tested and one was charged; on 10 Oct 2026, 31 of 102 guests at an unlicensed club on Khao San Road tested positive. A positive test is an offence. Since 23 Jun 2025 cannabis flower is a controlled herb: tourists may not buy, carry or use it without a Thai prescription, and walk-in shops may be operating illegally. E-cigarettes and vapes are banned; in a case reported in April 2026, two tourists paid a 40,000 THB fine after vaping on a beach. Licensed, well-known venues are a safer choice than new pop-up bars.

essentials.title: Scams and safety
essentials.text: The Grand Palace and the big temples are open every day. Anyone outside who says they are closed and offers a cheap tuk-tuk tour is running the gem-shop scam; the gems are cut glass. Use Grab, or insist on the meter in taxis, and agree tuk-tuk prices first. Do not ask drivers for bar tips: they take you where they get commission. Avoid bars you cannot see into from the street; drink spiking has been reported in some go-go bars. Keep phones and wallets in front pockets in the Chatuchak and Yaowarat crowds. Numbers: Tourist Police 1155 (English, 24 hours), police 191, ambulance 1669.

essentials.title: Weather and what to wear in January
essentials.text: January is the dry, cooler season: average highs about 33°C and lows about 23°C, with about 2 rainy days in the month (1991-2020 averages). Sunrise is about 06:45 and sunset about 18:05-18:15. Temples (Grand Palace, Wat Pho, Wat Arun, Golden Mount, Ayutthaya) need covered shoulders and knees: no tank tops, crop tops, see-through tops, shorts, mini skirts, or ripped, tight or cycling trousers. Pack light long trousers or a long skirt and a T-shirt with sleeves. For rooftops and clubs wear smart casual clothes and closed shoes, no flip-flops or singlets. Wear shoes with grip for the Wat Arun steps and the 344 steps of the Golden Mount.
